strings.Hinter dem Optimalset steckt das NTC, da: Behind the Optimal Set is the NTC, PM-International's Nutrient Transport Concept. The basic idea: there's a long way between taking in nutrients and actually using them. The NTC is designed to get nutrients in the right form, at the right time, to where your body needs them. There are 100+ patents behind it. On top of that comes the timing approach: certain products in the morning, others during the day or in the evening, because your body needs different nutrients at different times. That's the difference between a single supplement and a well-thought-out system.
No, these are food supplements. They are not a substitute for a balanced diet and not a medical treatment. If you have specific health concerns, please talk to a doctor first. What the Optimal Set does is supply your body better, not cure anything.
strings.Warum ist da Zucker drin?: Why is there sugar in it?
strings.Das ist eine Frage, die {{#unless team_m: {{#unless team_modus=team}}I{{/unless}}{{#if team_modus=team}}We{{/if}} get this question a lot, and the answer surprises many people. Yes, some products contain a small amount of sugar, dextrose for example. But it's not there to make it taste sweet. It works as a transport vehicle. Put simply: your gut has channels through which nutrients pass into the blood. Certain vitamins and amino acids get through those channels much better when a small amount of sugar comes along. The sugar basically opens the gate, and the nutrients slip in with it. The amount is so small that you don't need to worry about it, as long as you're not sipping it all day long.
strings.Womit ist das gesüßt, und was ist der Un: What is it sweetened with, and how is that different from other sweeteners?
strings.Viele FitLine-Produkte werden mit Stevia: Many FitLine products are sweetened with stevia. Stevia is a natural plant extract from the plant of the same name, has virtually zero calories and doesn't mess with your blood sugar. That might sound like the typical health trend, but the difference to classic sweeteners like aspartame or acesulfame K really matters: those are made synthetically and have been under debate for a while, because they're said to trigger cravings in some people or put strain on the gut. Stevia comes from nature and is considered safe in normal amounts. So you get the sweet taste without burdening your body.
strings.Nein. Auf Konservierungsstoffe wird bewu: No. Preservatives are deliberately left out. That works because the products come in small, airtight sealed daily sachets. The powder never touches air or moisture until you open it, so it simply doesn't need preserving. Once you open a sachet, you use it all at once. Nothing sits around half-open, nothing oxidizes, no preservatives needed.
strings.Ist das nicht schlecht für die Umwelt, w: Isn't all that single-serve packaging bad for the environment?
strings.Das ist eine faire Frage, und {{#unless: Fair question, and {{#unless team_modus=team}}I{{/unless}}{{#if team_modus=team}}we{{/if}} get the first thought: more packaging sounds like more waste. But look a little closer. A regular supplement jar holds 30 or 60 servings, needs drying agents and oxygen absorbers to stay stable, and you open it every day. The rest keeps oxidizing the whole time. The daily sachets here are sealed airtight, so they don't need any preservatives, and there's no waste from leftovers going bad. On top of that, the packaging is made from recyclable material. It's not perfect, of course, but compared directly it's more sustainable than all those big plastic bottles that end up in the bin half full.
